To attack an enemy, a participant makes an attack roll using the appropriate weapon or spell attack bonus. If the roll is equal to or greater than the targetʼs armor class, the attack hits, and the participant rolls for damage. Damage is subtracted from the targetʼs hit points. If a participantʼs hit points are reduced to zero or below, they are unconscious and dying. If a participant reaches negative hit points equal to their maximum hit points, they are dead.

An attack of opportunity is a combat mechanic used in D20-based TTRPGs like D&D. It allows a character to make a free melee attack against an opponent who provokes them by moving out of their threatened area. To use an attack of opportunity, the character must have a melee weapon in hand and be within range of the opponent. If an enemy moves out of the character's threatened area, the character can make an attack of opportunity against them using their normal attack bonus. This attack deals the same amount of damage as a normal melee attack. It's important to note that characters can only make one attack of opportunity per round, regardless of how many times their opponent moves within their threatened area. Additionally, certain actions, such as using the Disengage action, can prevent an opponent from triggering an attack of opportunity. Using attacks of opportunity effectively requires careful positioning and strategy. Characters must be aware of their threatened area and anticipate where opponents are likely to move. They must also be mindful of their own positioning to avoid leaving themselves open to attacks from other opponents. Attacks of opportunity can be a valuable asset for any combat-focused character in a D20-based TTRPG like D&D. They provide an additional opportunity for characters to deal damage and control the battlefield. However, they also require careful planning and execution to use effectively.
